chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Jundab, from Sufyan ibn al-Simt, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whenever Allah intends good for a servant, and he commits a sin, He follows it with an affliction and reminds him of seeking forgiveness; and whenever He intends evil for a servant, and he commits a sin, He follows it with a bounty to make him forget seeking forgiveness, and he continues to indulge in it.'
And this is the Word of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'We will gradually lead them on from where they do not know.'
With the bounties during the disobedience.

key_terms.سَنَسْتَدْرِجُهُمْ: We will gradually lead them on

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between how God treats the sins of those He intends good for versus those He intends evil for?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the concept of 'istidrāj' (gradual allurement), where divine blessings serve as a subtle trap to distract the sinner from repentance, whereas afflictions act as a merciful wake-up call. Rooted in Shia exegetical tradition, this mechanism highlights how God's intention—whether for ultimate salvation or continued misguidance—is revealed through the nature of the consequences following sin. It underscores the spiritual danger of comfort, which can lead to forgetfulness (ghaflah), contrasting it with the purifying effect of hardship.
